plain_english: Nick's India Stock Desk is a research screen for NSE stocks. It does not place trades and it does not connect to a broker. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell.

There are no option contract picks. The liquid stocks page is a stock screen. The put and call walls page is market mood only. Indian options use fixed lot sizes, so this desk does not pick a contract.
Prices are in rupees. They come from Yahoo Finance using the .NS ticker. The benchmark is the Nifty 50. Bank Nifty is shown next to it.

Each money measure is plus 1, 0, or minus 1 versus that company's own recent history. Lower is better for forward P/E, trailing P/E, price/sales, debt/equity, and price/free cash flow. Higher is better for revenue growth, EPS growth, return on equity, and dividend yield. Analyst rating can be plus 2 to minus 2. Shareholding, insiders, the price trend, the oscillator, the latest result, and the sector each add a small point. The score is the sum of the points we actually have.
A missing number is left blank and marked n/a. It is not stored as zero and it does not add or subtract a point. If a free source is blocked, the page says not available.
Free data does not include a history of forward estimates. The baseline for forward P/E is the 3-year average of year-end trailing P/E.
The industry figure is the middle value of the other stocks in the same sector on this desk. It is not a paid database. If fewer than four peers have a number, the comparison is blank.

BUY, HOLD, and AVOID are research labels. A high score that is extended, in a downtrend, or missing most of its financials is labeled HOLD instead of BUY. Entry, stop, and target are a plan for study, not an order.

You will see an analyst target when Yahoo has one, a price/free-cash-flow target, a PEG-style target, and a blend of whichever of those exist. The trade target is separate. It is an entry-zone plan using the recent daily range.

Once a month the job asks what the score would have been using only data that was already public, then looks at the next 1, 4, and 12 weeks versus the Nifty 50. Read the headline. If it says there is no clear edge, believe that. Past results are not future results.

Promoter, FII, DII, and other public percents come from the NSE shareholding filing when that file is reachable. The change is versus the prior quarter. If the split is missing, the cell says not verified. It is not a US 13F report.
Insider points use NSE PIT buy and sell counts over three months. If NSE blocks the file, the page says data not available for free and the score for that piece stays blank.

The put/call line is Nifty put open interest divided by call open interest, when the NSE option chain answers. Walls are the strikes with the most open interest. They are mood, not a trade. If NSE blocks the chain, the page says not available.
There is no Indian version of the AAII survey, so that survey is not shown. This page uses India VIX and, when the NSE file answers, the day's FII and DII cash flow in crores.
There is no free official daily Nifty 50 P/E this desk can rely on. The chart is the median trailing P/E of the stocks on this desk. The official column stays blank.

The macro page shows India CPI, GDP, and industry growth from the World Bank when that feed answers, plus the rupee from Yahoo. A forecast is often missing, so the surprise stays blank. It is a sketch, not a forecast. The rate column on the sector map is a simple rule of thumb.
This is the Nifty Auto index divided by the Nifty FMCG index. It stands in for the old discretionary versus staples chart. Above the 50-day average of the ratio is labeled risk on.

Prices are downloaded in batches. Hourly runs only fetch the latest bars and keep the saved history. Statements, ratings, shareholding, insider counts, and option chains refresh at most once a day. If a source fails, the previous file is kept and the updates log says CACHED.

The desk scores the Nifty 50, the Nifty Next 50, and the Nifty Midcap 150. A stock in more than one list appears once. Each list has an on/off switch in config.json. Your holdings and watchlist are always included.
Times are shown in India time (IST) and Pacific time (PT).

This page follows the same 8-point trend template and contraction count as Nick's indicator, with the Nifty 50 as the benchmark. READY means 8 of 8 and price is still under the buy point. BROKEN OUT today means today's close crossed that point on big volume.

C and A are the year-ago EPS change from the saved statements. N is how close the price is to its 52-week closing high. S is the 20-day average volume. L is the relative-strength percentile versus the Nifty inside this universe. I is the shareholding change when we have it. M is the Nifty, and Bank Nifty when that price is already on file. A blank that says not verified was not in the cache. It is not a guess.
A box is a tight sideways range that closes out the top on above-average volume. A flag is a sharp rise, a short pause, then a close above the pause on volume. These two are desk rules.
Leaders puts a VCP that is ready or broken out today together with a strict CANSLIM qualify. One row per stock.

Edit input/holdings.csv and input/my_watchlist.csv to change the portfolio and the watchlist. Example rows are marked example=yes. Replace them with your own shares and cost. The desk still will not place a trade.
The alerts page lists score and label changes since the last run. It does not send a phone alert, an email, or a message.

OK means the source answered. PARTIAL means a column is blank on every row. CACHED means this run failed and an older copy was used. MISSING means there is no copy at all. A blank cell is missing data. It is not a zero.
Every page has an on/off switch in config.json under features. The index lists have switches under indexes. Turning a page off keeps the file headers so the site does not break.
